settings.title: Understanding Skin Brightness & Glow
settings.content:
"Glow" isn't just a marketing term - it reflects the condition of the skin's surface. Skin looks luminous when its surface is smooth, well-hydrated and even in tone. When the complexion looks uneven, dead cells accumulate, or oxidative stress dulls the surface, skin can lose its natural radiance.

True radiance is about supporting the look of an even, healthy-looking complexion: a more even-looking tone, strong antioxidant defence, healthy-looking cell turnover and good hydration.

settings.title: What Causes Dull, Uneven Skin?
settings.content:
Uneven-Looking Tone
UV exposure, hormonal changes and everyday stress can leave the complexion looking uneven, with the appearance of dark spots and patchiness that becomes more noticeable with age.

Oxidative Stress
Free radicals from UV, pollution and blue light stress the skin and dull its surface. As the skin's antioxidant reserves (especially glutathione) decline with age, this dullness builds up faster.

Slow Cell Turnover
Dead surface cells sit on the skin longer as turnover slows from around 28 days (age 20) to 40-60 days (age 50+). This creates a dull, uneven-looking appearance.

Everyday Stress on the Skin
Marks left after blemishes or irritation, plus daily environmental stress, can make the complexion look less even over time.

settings.title: The Antioxidant Approach to Brightening
settings.content:
Many traditional brightening approaches are harsh and can leave the skin looking irritated. Glutathione takes a gentler, antioxidant-led approach.

As the body's master antioxidant, glutathione helps defend the skin against the oxidative stress that dulls the complexion, supporting a brighter, more even-looking tone over time. Combined with stable vitamin C and supporting peptides, this approach helps brighten the look of the skin while keeping it comfortable and strong.

settings.title: Understanding Collagen & Skin Plumping
settings.content:
Collagen is the most abundant protein in your body and the primary structural component of your skin. It forms a dense network in the dermis that gives skin its thickness, volume, and plump appearance. When collagen levels are high, skin looks full, smooth, and youthful. When collagen declines, skin becomes thinner, loses volume, and develops a hollow, aged appearance.

"Skin plumping" refers to restoring this lost volume - not through temporary surface effects, but through genuine rebuilding of the collagen matrix from within.

settings.title: Why Does Collagen Decline?
settings.content:
Age-Related Decline
Collagen production decreases by 1-1.5% per year from your mid-20s. By age 60, you have lost 40-60% of your skin's collagen. Women lose up to 30% in the first five years post-menopause.

UV-Induced Destruction
UV radiation is the largest external factor. UVA rays break collagen cross-links and activate MMPs - enzymes that digest collagen fibers. A single significant sun exposure elevates MMP activity for days.

Free Radicals and Glycation
Free radicals from UV, pollution, and smoking fragment collagen. Sugar molecules attach to collagen (glycation), forming AGEs that make fibers permanently stiff and brittle.

Inflammation and HA Loss
Chronic inflammation upregulates collagen-destroying MMPs. Meanwhile, Hyaluronic Acid production drops roughly 50% by age 40 - without adequate hydration, the collagen matrix becomes compressed and less effective.

settings.title: The Peptide Approach to Collagen Rebuilding
settings.content:
Collagen supplements must survive digestion - absorption is variable. Topical collagen molecules are too large (300,000 daltons) to penetrate the skin. Neither reaches the deeper skin directly.

Peptides take a fundamentally different approach. Small enough to penetrate the skin (under 1,000 daltons), they are associated with the skin's natural collagen activity. When combined with Hyaluronic Acid for immediate hydration and copper peptide for broad support, this creates one of the most comprehensive topical approaches to firmer, plumper-looking skin.

Clinical Evidence
Matrixyl 3000 supported a reduced appearance of deep wrinkles and improved skin tonicity in manufacturer studies. Laboratory (in-vitro) tests showed a significant increase in collagen production in cultured cells. Our formula delivers a generous level of active peptides.

The HA Advantage
Hyaluronic Acid holds 1,000x its weight in water, providing immediate plumping while Matrixyl 3000 supports the look of firmer skin underneath.

Best For: Volume loss, thinning-looking skin, dehydration lines and long-term firmness support.

GHK-Cu is one of the most-studied peptides in skin science. It is valued for supporting the appearance of firmness, elasticity and a smoother, plumper-looking complexion. Few other peptides have been studied as extensively.

settings.title: Understanding Fine Lines & Wrinkles
settings.content:
Fine lines and wrinkles are among the earliest and most visible signs of skin aging. Fine lines are shallow creases, typically less than 1mm deep, that first appear around the eyes, forehead, and mouth. Over time, they deepen into wrinkles - permanent folds that become visible even when your face is completely relaxed.

While wrinkles are a natural part of aging, understanding the biology behind them reveals why some people develop them earlier - and what can be done to slow, prevent, and even reverse them.

settings.title: What Causes Fine Lines & Wrinkles?
settings.content:
Collagen and Elastin Breakdown
Starting around age 25, your body produces approximately 1% less collagen per year. By age 50, most people have lost 30-50% of their total skin collagen. Skin gradually loses its ability to spring back from facial expressions.

Repetitive Muscle Movement
Every facial expression creates a temporary fold in the skin. As the collagen matrix weakens, expression lines on the forehead, crow's feet, and between the eyebrows become permanently etched - these muscles contract thousands of times per day.

UV Radiation (Photoaging)
UV exposure is responsible for up to 80% of visible facial aging. UVA rays penetrate deep into the dermis where they generate free radicals that directly break down collagen and elastin fibers.

Glycation and Dehydration
Sugar molecules attach to collagen proteins forming AGEs, making fibers stiff and brittle. Meanwhile, Hyaluronic Acid production drops roughly 50% by your 40s.

settings.title: The Peptide Approach to Wrinkle Reduction
settings.content:
Traditional anti-wrinkle treatments address symptoms but often miss root causes. Retinoids increase cell turnover but can cause irritation. In-clinic treatments act on muscle movement but require repeat appointments.

Peptides offer a different approach: they work with your skin's own biology. Signal peptides support the skin's natural collagen activity. Other peptides help visibly relax the look of expression lines. Combined, they help soften the look of existing wrinkles and support smoother-looking skin over time - without irritation or downtime.

settings.content:
How It Works
Acetyl Hexapeptide-8, applied topically, is valued for helping to visibly relax the look of expression lines around the eyes and forehead for a smoother appearance.

Clinical Evidence
In a randomized, placebo-controlled trial, Acetyl Hexapeptide-8 delivered 48.9% overall anti-wrinkle efficacy versus 0% for placebo (Wang 2013). Improvement in the appearance of wrinkles builds gradually over several weeks.

Best For: Expression lines on the forehead, crow's feet, frown lines and smile lines.

settings.title: Matrixyl 3000 + HA - Rebuild the Collagen Matrix

settings.title: Understanding Skin Firmness & Density
settings.content:
Skin firmness depends on two structural proteins: collagen (which provides strength and structure) and elastin (which allows skin to snap back after stretching). Together with glycosaminoglycans like hyaluronic acid, they form the extracellular matrix - the scaffolding that keeps skin plump, firm, and resilient.

After age 30, collagen production declines 1-1.5% per year while existing collagen degrades faster. The result: skin that feels thinner, less bouncy, and increasingly prone to sagging - especially along the jawline, cheeks, and neck.

settings.title: What Causes Loss of Firmness?
settings.content:
Collagen Degradation
MMPs (matrix metalloproteinases) break down collagen faster than your body can replace it. UV exposure, inflammation, and pollution accelerate MMP activity dramatically.

Elastin Fragmentation
Unlike collagen, elastin is barely replaced after adolescence. Once damaged, elastic fibers fragment and cannot reassemble properly - leading to permanent loss of skin bounce and resilience.

Fat Pad Redistribution
Facial fat pads that provide youthful volume shift downward with gravity and reduce in size, contributing to hollow cheeks and a less defined jawline.

Hormonal Changes
During menopause, estrogen decline causes a 30% loss of skin collagen in the first five years. This rapid structural loss explains why skin firmness changes noticeably during this period.

Glutathione (GSH) is a tripeptide composed of three amino acids: glutamic acid, cysteine, and glycine. It is the most abundant intracellular antioxidant in the human body, present in virtually every cell. In skincare, glutathione is valued for two reasons: it helps neutralise free radicals that contribute to a dull, tired-looking complexion, and it is associated with a brighter, more even-looking skin tone.

Topical glutathione has gained significant interest in skincare for supporting a brighter, more even-looking skin tone and radiance, and for helping protect the skin against UV-induced oxidative stress that can dull the complexion over time.

Acetyl Hexapeptide-8 (acetyl hexapeptide-3) is a synthetic peptide first described by researchers at Lipotec (now Lubrizol). It is one of the most popular peptides in modern anti-wrinkle skincare, valued for helping to visibly relax the look of expression lines around the eyes and forehead.

settings.title: 48.9% Overall Anti-Wrinkle Efficacy vs Placebo
settings.content:
A randomized, placebo-controlled trial examined the anti-wrinkle effects of topical Acetyl Hexapeptide-8 applied twice daily to the periorbital region (crow's feet area).

Study design: RCT, placebo-controlled, 60 subjects (3:1 ratio), 4 weeks, twice daily application

Key results:

  • 48.9% total anti-wrinkle efficacy in the Acetyl Hexapeptide-8 group vs 0% in placebo
  • All objective roughness parameters decreased significantly (p < 0.01)

Wang Y et al. (2013). American Journal of Clinical Dermatology. View on PubMed

settings.title: Up to ~30% Softer-Looking Wrinkle Depth in 30 Days
settings.content:
An early study by the peptide's developers combined laboratory (in-vitro) mechanism data with a small in-use test of an Acetyl Hexapeptide-8 emulsion.

Study design: Combined in-vitro + in-use proof-of-concept, healthy female volunteers, 30 days.

Key results:

  • Up to ~30% reduction in measured wrinkle depth after 30 days (early proof-of-concept by the developers)
  • Supported the appearance of smoother skin around the eyes over 30 days

Blanes-Mira C et al. (2002). International Journal of Cosmetic Science. View on PubMed

settings.title: 14.6% Improvement in Just 5 Days
settings.content:
A double-blind, randomized trial tested microneedle patches containing Acetyl Hexapeptide-8 against patches alone on 52 Korean female subjects using a split-face design.

Study design: Double-blind RCT, split-face, 52 subjects, 29 days

Key results:

  • 14.6% fine wrinkle improvement vs 5.9% for patch alone (p < 0.05)
  • 13.6% deep wrinkle improvement vs 3.5% for patch alone
  • Statistically significant results within just 5 days

An JH et al. (2019). Annals of Dermatology. View study

settings.title: Understanding Skin Repair & Renewal
settings.content:
Your skin renews itself approximately every 28 days through a constant cycle of cell turnover. But this renewal cycle slows with age - by your 50s, the cycle stretches to 40-60 days. The result: a duller complexion, accumulated signs of environmental stress and a loss of the "glow" associated with youthful-looking skin.

Supporting the look of renewed skin goes deeper than surface exfoliation. It's about supporting the skin's own renewal so it looks firmer, smoother and more revitalised, and helping defend it against the UV and environmental stress that speed up visible aging.

settings.title: What Slows Skin Repair?
settings.content:
Slower Renewal
As we age, the skin's natural renewal cycle slows, so dull surface cells linger longer and the complexion looks tired and less radiant.

Environmental Stress
UV and pollution place daily stress on the skin. Younger skin copes with this well, but over time the visible effects build up - a rougher texture, uneven tone and loss of glow.

Loss of Firmness
The skin's support structures weaken with age, so it can look less firm and less bouncy, with more visible fine lines.

Reduced Resilience
Everyday stress on the skin gradually makes the complexion look less resilient and slower to bounce back, which is why supportive, revitalising skincare becomes more important with age.

settings.title: The Renewal Approach
settings.content:
Rather than forcing faster cell turnover through chemical exfoliation (which can thin the skin), renewal-focused skincare supports the skin's own natural processes. PDRN (Polydeoxyribonucleotide) - salmon-derived polynucleotides - and copper peptide GHK-Cu are both valued in skin science for supporting a firmer, smoother and more revitalised-looking complexion.

This approach supports the look of healthy, renewed skin as part of a routine, for deeper, more lasting-looking results.

settings.title: What is PDRN?
settings.content: PDRN (Polydeoxyribonucleotide) is a polynucleotide extracted from purified salmon DNA (INCI: Sodium DNA). It interacts with the adenosine A2A receptor, a pathway associated with the skin's renewal-related activity, and is valued for a firmer, smoother and more revitalised-looking complexion.

settings.title: Is salmon DNA safe on my skin?
settings.content: Yes. The extraction process removes all proteins and potential allergens, leaving only purified polynucleotides. PDRN has a well-documented safety profile, with no adverse effects reported in published studies.

settings.title: How is this different from retinol?
settings.content: Retinol forces faster cell turnover from outside, causing irritation and sun sensitivity. PDRN activates your own repair machinery from within - no irritation, no purging, no photosensitivity. They work through completely different mechanisms and can be combined.

settings.title: Can I use this after cosmetic procedures?
settings.content: PDRN-based skincare is gentle and well tolerated. If you have recently had a professional skin treatment, always follow your practitioner's specific aftercare advice first before introducing any new product.

settings.title: Why is Oligopeptide-1 included?

settings.title: Can topical collagen actually firm skin?
settings.content: This cream uses a triple collagen approach: hydrolyzed collagen (small enough to penetrate), soluble collagen (forms a moisture-retaining film), and native collagen (structural support). Combined with signal peptides that stimulate your own collagen production.

settings.title: What does Elastin do in this formula?
settings.content: Elastin is the protein that gives skin its bounce and snap-back. Unlike collagen (strength), elastin provides flexibility. After adolescence, your body barely produces new elastin - topical supplementation helps restore skin resilience.

settings.title: Morning or evening use?
settings.content: Both work well. Morning: use as your moisturiser before SPF. Evening: use after your serums as a nourishing overnight treatment. For maximum firming, use twice daily.

settings.title: How is this different from the Copper Peptide Night Cream?
settings.content: The Night Cream focuses on repair (GHK-Cu, Centella Asiatica, barrier-repair lipids). This cream focuses on structural firming (triple collagen, elastin, signal peptides). Choose based on your primary concern - or alternate between them.

settings.title: Will this help my jawline and neck?
settings.content: Yes. Loss of firmness along the jawline and neck is primarily caused by collagen and elastin depletion. Apply with upward strokes from collarbone to jawline for best results.
